## CHANGES-v2.7 (I2 withdrawn: `lookup` records a Point per returned row)

| # | Item | Verdict | What v2.7 does | Where |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| J1 | the gap I2 closed: a `lookup` whose rows change V at the same J must re-run | **the orchestrator's alternative wins on the figures; I2 is withdrawn** | **Rule.** `lookup` records its index `Span` when it is made, and the cursor records `Point(table id ‖ Key[K])` for each row it returns, when it returns it. A put that changes V at the same J hits that Point, and a row that enters or leaves the J range hits the Span. Index entries keep empty values. A `put` whose old and new index keys are byte-equal writes no index entry (the landed source removes and re-inserts it, `put_impl:1318–1325`). **What makes it possible:** the per-row Points must reach the Tx's read log, and today's `Rows` is `send` and outlives the Tx, which is why v2.6 called this impossible. So `lookup` now returns a scoped cursor, `IndexRows[K, V]`, anchored to the Tx (OWN-20) and holding the Tx's `View[Log[Read]]`, as `Tx` itself does. RUN `programs-v27/`: `ixrows_ok`, a body that iterates it and records each Point, is ACCEPTED, and so is `ixrows_generic`, a generic scoped cursor. `ixrows_escape`, a body that returns it, is REFUSED (LANG-13). `ixrows_write`, a `put` while the cursor lives, is REFUSED (OWN-10). **That last one is the cost:** a body must finish iterating a lookup, collecting what it needs, before it writes. `range`, `scan` and `find` keep their `send` `Rows`, because a range's Span covers every value in it up front, and a Snapshot read has no read set. | §1.3, §1.10, §2.4, §1.11, L26 |
| J1a | write side: instructions per put, one put per commit, J unchanged, ~100,000 rows | **ESTIMATE**, from RUN parts | Parts (callgrind of R1, LLVM release): the data-tree insert is 50,460 Ir per call (5,046,228,305 over 100,000 calls); `put_bytes` is 53,851 per call; one R1 commit is 98,800; one `get` with decode is 3,875 (R3); an index key build is about 1,000 (ESTIMATE). Rows: **0 indexes:** 98.8k either way (+3.9k for I4's old-row get, either way). **1 index:** I2 158.6k, Points **104.7k**, landed today 209k (remove plus insert). **3 indexes:** I2 270.3k, Points **108.7k**, landed today 422k. I2 adds one index-entry insert (about 54k) per index per put. Points adds only the key compare. | — |
| J1b | read side: lookup returning 1, 100 and 10,000 rows (8-byte K) | **ESTIMATE** | **Read-set bytes:** I2, one Span of about 100 B for any count. Points, 100 B + 48 B per row (a `Bytes` handle of 24, 16 bytes of key, an 8-byte tag): **148 B, 4.9 KB, 480 KB**. **Recording:** about 400 Ir per row (one key copy and an append), against a lookup's own per-row cost of about 4k (index step, primary get, decode), so about +10%. **Publisher:** each read-set entry is one more interval-index entry, so inserting a re-run's Points costs O(r log E), and each Change still costs O(log E). I2 instead adds one Change per index per put to every commit on an indexed table, which the publisher matches whether or not anyone subscribes, and `changes` walks them. **The runner's Cover does not hold these keys:** `cover(Shape, lo, hi)` holds table ranges a query only names, not rows it read (RUNNER-SPEC §4), so the Points are new state, charged to the session budget with the rest of the read set (§3). | — |
| J1c | correctness under L26 | **both sound; Points is exact** | **Keys-only lookup:** the API has none. Every lookup returns (K, V). Were one added, it would record no Points, since K is in the index key. **A row deleted and re-put at the same J in one commit:** the index key is unchanged, and the primary key's value differs between a and b only if V changed, which then hits the Point. Same V means no Change, and the answer is the same. I2 would re-run spuriously here. **"Unique" index:** the store has no unique kind; every entry is index id ‖ J ‖ K (§2.4), so an extractor that happens to give distinct J values is the same case. **Partial iteration:** Points cover only the rows returned, which are all the body saw. The rows after them are covered for membership by the Span, and their values were never read. | L26 |
| J1d | `changes` and compaction | **Points: no change. I2: more of both.** | Under Points, an unchanged-J put writes no index node. `changes`, the incremental checkpoint (L5's k(2h+1) per written key) and copy-forward all see fewer nodes than under the landed source. Under I2, every put rewrites one entry per index, so each index adds one Change to `changes` and 2h+1 nodes to the next checkpoint. | — |
| J1e | reversibility | — | No disk byte depends on it (index values stay empty). The API change is `lookup`'s result type: `IndexRows` scoped to the Tx, with `next_indexed`. Going back to I2 would restore a `send` cursor and add the stamp before S2 writes packs. After S2, the stamp would be a format change. | — |

## CHANGES-v2.6 (S1 review: read-set encoding, stale read handles, overwrite accounting)

| # | Item | Verdict | What v2.6 does | Where |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| I1 | read-set encoding (review: `fetch_bytes:436` records the bare user key, `range_bytes:523–527` and `lookup:1436–1439` record tree keys) | **one encoding: data-tree keys, the same bytes as `Change.tree_key`** | `Read = Point(Bytes) \| Span(Bytes, Bytes)`. Every key is a data-tree key (§2.4): table id u32 BE ‖ `Key[K]`, or index id u32 BE ‖ `Key[J]` ‖ `Key[K]`. A Span is [lo, hi) in byte order: `Unbounded` low is the id's 4-byte prefix, `Unbounded` high is the prefix of id + 1, an `Included` high bound is its key ‖ 0x00, and an `Excluded` low bound is its key ‖ 0x00 (the prefix-free key format makes these exact). The u32 id is dropped from `Read`: it is the key's first four bytes, so keeping it would give two copies of one fact. **The publisher's test is a byte compare:** a Change hits a read set when its `tree_key` equals a Point or lies in a Span. | §1.3, §1.5, L15, L26 |
| I2 | `lookup` read sets missed value changes (found while settling I1) | **WITHDRAWN in v2.7 (J1).** Was: index entries carry the row's write version | `lookup` records only the index Span, and it returns primary values. An index entry's value was empty, so a `put` that changed V without changing J changed no key in that Span, and a live lookup would never re-run. Now an index entry's value is the version (u64 BE) of the commit that last wrote its row. Every `put` rewrites the row's index entries, so any write of a row is a Change inside every index Span that holds it. A same-value rewrite also shows up, as `changes` already counts it in k (H4). Cost: 8 accounted bytes per index entry (+94 B/row in §1.11's table, was +86). The alternative, recording a Point per returned row, is impossible: `Rows` outlives the Tx. Recording the table's whole span would re-run every lookup on every write to the table. Nothing is on disk yet, so this changes no stored byte. | §1.3, §2.4, §1.11, L26 |
| I3 | stale read handles (review: writes check the epoch at `writable:1276–1290`; `fetch`, `get` and `find` check identity only) | **a read checks that its handle's id is live in the catalog of the state it reads** | A table or index **id is an incarnation**. Ids come from the one `next_table` counter and are never reused. `create_table` after `drop_table` gives a new id, and **`migrate` (row 13, S4) now gives the table and each of its indexes new ids**. Every read (`fetch`, `range`, `lookup`, `get`, `scan`, `find`, and all three inside `look`) first looks up the handle's catalog key in **the catalog tree of the roots it reads** (the Tx's, or the Snapshot's). If the entry is absent, or holds another id, the read is `Stale(id)`. So against a current Tx, a handle from before a drop is `Stale`, never an empty read. Against an old Snapshot that still holds the table, the same handle reads its rows, because that snapshot's catalog lists the id, and a handle made after the drop is `Stale` there. **Shape and Index carry no epoch.** The epoch guards only index completeness, which only writes need (§1.2). A Shape or Index carries its id and catalog key. A schema number appended after a handle was resolved remains `Stale` row by row, as before. Cost: at most one catalog lookup per read call, not per row (R1 measures it). A handle keeps the catalog root page it was resolved against when that root is one leaf with no BLOB cell, and that page lists the handle's id under its key. A read whose catalog root has the same bytes skips the lookup, because a lookup in such a leaf reads only its bytes. | §1.2, §1.5, §1.12, L16 |
| I4 | admission on overwrite (review: `put_bytes:463–465` adds on overwrite, and a memory store has no checkpoint) | **exact where nothing shares the old row; settled before any refusal** | (a) While the store has no pin and no branch but main, an overwrite subtracts the old row's entry (the put already reaches it), and a delete subtracts its own. The account is then exact after every commit, in both modes. A memory store that overwrites one key forever keeps a constant account. (b) While a pin or another branch exists, overwrites and deletes subtract nothing, and the excess is settled at cuts. **A memory store makes cuts too:** `checkpoint` and the `checkpoint_bytes` trigger run the reference count and write no file. (c) **Before refusing a commit while the account holds unsettled charges, `run` settles it first.** A memory store counts inline. A disk store waits for a checkpoint's ack. Then `run` checks again, so a refusal always rests on the exact figure. That wait comes before publish and changes nothing, so a cancel there leaves the store as it was (§3.7). (a) is S1; (b) and (c) are S4 with pins and forks. | §1.3, §1.11, §3.7, L27 |
| I5 | the review's "What S2 must change" | **noted for S2's format review** | Checked against the S2 diff when 1010 stops before landing it: the placeholders `open = 0` and `sequence = 1` (`memory_at:169`, `snapshot:181`, tickets at 307 and 1626) are replaced by the persisted identity, the open number and restored node and table counters; `schema_publish:1613–1627` goes through the manifest protocol (§1.2 "Schema commits", §3.5); `close:350–365` follows §1.10's five steps and returns the first stored error, not ignoring join results; frame binding uses real file offsets and is recomputed on copy-forward. | §1.10, §3.5, §7 |

## CHANGES-v2.5 (two S2 gaps: an oversized NODE, unnamed packs after a crash)

| # | Item | Verdict | What v2.5 does | Where |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | a NODE larger than `Options.pack_bytes` (1010's gap 1: `pack_bytes = 1`, one legal row, a checkpoint) | **ALLOWED: the NODE goes in a pack alone; the option is not refused** | A NODE goes into the open pack unless it would take the pack past `pack_bytes` and the pack already holds a NODE; in that case the pack closes first. **Bound:** a pack file is at most max(`pack_bytes`, 72 + 16 + the NODE payload limit). At the fixed limits that is max(`pack_bytes`, **33,686,116 bytes**): 72 for the HEADER file, 16 for the frame head, and 33,686,028 for the payload (§2.7). The 64 MiB default is above it, so with the defaults every pack is at most `pack_bytes`. This is the exception `group_bytes` already has (§3.3), so like things are treated alike. Refusing the option would add an Error case and a validation that hang on the limits, and would protect nothing. **Recovery** reads a pack whole as before; open's transient peak is the account plus the largest pack, so the same max. **Compaction:** a one-NODE pack's live bytes are all or nothing, so it is never copied forward; it is retired when its NODE dies. A NODE is never split across packs. | §1.1, §1.11, §2.5, §3.5 |
| H2 | unnamed packs after a crash (1010's gap 2, with a second crash during cleanup leaving a gap) | **v2.4 was safe but stated the wrong reason; the rule is now naming, not cleanup** | **Safety rule:** a MANIFEST lists only packs that its own cut wrote. A cut writes its packs at seq `next_pack`, `next_pack + 1`, … of the manifest it starts from. Each pack is written as `p-<seq>.tmp` with `Write` (which truncates), synced, and renamed onto `p-<seq>`, replacing any file of that name (W2 rename over an existing name, landed 1070c6a3). So a stale `p-x` left by an unpublished cut always has x ≥ `next_pack`, and it is replaced before any manifest lists x. Open loads only listed packs. **Cleanup is best effort and only frees space:** after the O1 directory sync, open removes `MANIFEST.tmp`, then `p-x` and `p-x.tmp` for x = `next_pack`, `next_pack + 1`, … until both names are NotFound, then the retired packs. Cleanup itself issues no directory sync. A pack it misses because of a gap is replaced by a later cut, or removed by a later open once a gap closes. **Space bound:** the leftover p-files are at most the packs of the largest unpublished cut. **No directory listing is needed**, and none is asked for. | §2.6, §3.4, §3.5, §3.6, L25 |
| H3 | the model | **new, clean** | `model_v25_packs.py`. Its file system keeps **any subset** of the pending directory operations at a crash, which is weaker than the W2 provider's all-or-nothing restart and is the persistence 1010 named. Unsynced data is lost. The scenario: cut A writes three packs, one an oversized NODE alone, with a crash after every step; recovery's cleanup runs with a second crash after every one of its steps; then cut B (one pack) and cut C (three packs) run, with every subset of their unsynced removals. Checks: P1, each listed pack is the content its cut wrote; P2, nothing unlisted is loaded; P3, unlisted, unretired p-files only at or above `next_pack`; P4, the pack size bound. RUN: **155 states, 7,556 crash cuts, 0 failures.** Mutants, all CAUGHT: `adopt_by_probe` (open loads what it finds), `skip_existing` (a cut lists a stale `p-x` without rewriting it; this is 1010's collision), `no_dir_sync` (no `sync_dir` between the pack renames and the MANIFEST), `start_below` (a cut starts below `next_pack`), and `close_after` (the pack closes after the NODE that passes `pack_bytes`). | §3.9 |
| H4 | `changes` bound (1010, accepted by the orchestrator) | **corrected** | Equal node ids are skipped, so a key rewritten with the same value is still visited. The bound is O(k log n) node visits for k keys written between the two snapshots, same-value rewrites included; w ≤ k changes are returned. | §1.5, F6 |
| H5 | format | **no byte changes** | MANIFEST's `next_pack` keeps its field and meaning; only its comment changes. | §2.6 |

## CHANGES-v2.4 (N11, `info` in `look`, slices, ENDSTATE)

| # | Item | Verdict | What v2.4 does | Where |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| G1 | N11: keep a call's record with its reply when the body returns a typed error | **ACCEPTED** | v2.3 was wrong here. Under v2.3 a typed error's reply frame had no record, so `tapes check` read every typed error as `NotRecorded`, while a fault was re-executable through the runner's reply-only commit. That is backwards: a typed error is a decision the body made, and it is the more useful one to re-check. On `Aborted`, the call section is now kept in the reply's streams-only frame. With no `reply` call, the record is discarded with everything else. §2.4 already allows that frame, since a call section needs only its stream's op in the same frame, so the format does not change. Each outcome kind under this rule, as a tape check sees it, is in the table below. Model: law G added (a frame has a call record iff it has a reply written by a run that ran an entry; the runner's reply-only `Failed(Gone)` commit for a removed entry is a run with a reply and no record, K3). RUN: **1,851 states, 2,396 cuts, 0 failures**. Mutants `abort_drops_call` (v2.3's rule) and `call_without_reply` are CAUGHT, and so are the four from v2.3. | §1.3, §2.4, L24, §3.9 |
| G2 | `info` inside `look` (store-build-1010's question; the orchestrator's interim ruling: a fault) | **REFUSED AT CHECK TIME instead: `info(mut tx: Tx)`** | A program that cannot mean anything should not type-check; a run-time `Failed` would leave a check to keep and a law case to test. RUN `programs-v24/` at 1f9148af: `info(mut tx)` inside a `look` body is REFUSED, OWN-5 "`tx` is not writable" (`info_look_mut`). It is ACCEPTED in a `run` body (`info_run_mut`) and in a helper that takes `mut Tx` (`info_helper_mut`). The old `info(tx: Tx)` is ACCEPTED inside `look` (`info_look_view`), which is the hole. Nothing a view-Tx body needs is lost: only `look` hands out a view Tx, and it has no CallInfo to give. The one cost is that a read-only helper that wants CallInfo must take `mut Tx`. L22 gains no case, because the refusal is the checker's. | §1.3, §1.5, §1.7 |
| G3 | slices (store-build-1010's reading) | **1010 is right; §7 stands** | S1.1 carries only §7's S1 items: Shape reads, `Aborted(Undone)`, `look` and `changes`. `record`, `reply`, S7 and the call section stay in S5 and S3, and **L24 is an S3 law**. A `memory` store has no journal, so `recorded` there is always None and a tape check reports `Unknown(StateGone)`. No record is kept in memory, because nothing would bound it. | §1.3, §7 |
| G4 | ENDSTATE `storage` passages that this spec makes wrong | **written** | `STORE-ENDSTATE-TEXT.md`, in the runner's form. Later items (rows 11 and 12, authorities, levels, followers) are kept and marked later. | — |

**What a tape check reports, by outcome (G1).** Verdict names are RUNNER-SPEC §7's.

| Outcome of the position's run | What the store committed | Call record | `tapes check` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Committed` | data, reply and call section, in one frame | yes | `Same`, or `Different(Reply)` / `Different(Writes)` |
| `Aborted(u)` with a `reply` call | reply and call section, one streams-only frame; no data | yes (G1) | `Same` when the re-run also returns the error and the same reply bytes, with no writes; otherwise `Different(Reply)` |
| `Aborted(u)` without a `reply` call | nothing | none | nothing to check: no version exists, and the position re-runs as `Abandoned` |
| `Failed(causes)` | nothing from the body; the runner then commits a reply-only `Failed` with its own `record` | yes, in the runner's commit | `Same` when the re-run faults the same way, else `Different(Reply)` |
| `Refused(c)` | nothing | none | nothing to check: the position re-runs |
| a gone entry's reply-only `Failed(Gone)` | reply only | none | `Unknown(NoEntry)` |
| a record whose version a cut taken by this Db covers (W2), or in a `memory` store | — | `recorded` is None | `Unknown(StateGone)` |

## CHANGES-v2.3 (reconciliation with RUNNER-SPEC v2, runner-spec-1020)

The runner's needs are followups.md "runner-spec-1020 -> store-spec-1001" N1–N6 (N7–N10 are not the store's). RUNNER-SPEC v2 §§1–4, 7 and 9 govern.

| # | Item | Verdict | What v2.3 does | Where |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | N1, rule S7: `admit(latest + 1)` while latest is admitted and unreplied | **ACCEPTED as written** | That admit is `Rejected(latest)` and commits nothing. A stream passes a position only after the position's reply is in the store, so `Rejected(l)` with `p < l` proves that p has a reply. RUNNER H4 and its `Superseded` answer rely on that proof. v2.2 committed `Admitted(latest + 1)` there; that is the hole the runner's mutant `store_v22_admit` shows (RUN at 1e866455: CAUGHT, "Superseded for p0 never replied"). With D6, an earlier open's unreplied latest p makes p+1 wait until p is re-sent and re-run (`Abandoned`). (v2.24, AH2: below latest is now `HistoryUnavailable`; `Rejected(l)` always has `p` > l.) | §1.8, L13 |
| F2 | N2, the runner's D3: a typed error in one commit | **ACCEPTED**, with what it is worth stated | `Aborted(A)` becomes `Aborted(Undone[A])`, where `Undone[A] { value: A, ticket: Option[Ticket] }`. On `Error(a)` the body's data writes are discarded. Its `reply` writes are committed as **one COMMIT frame with only a streams section**, and `ticket` names that commit. With no `reply` call, nothing is committed and `ticket` is None. That frame is already valid under §2.4: the section count was 1–2, so **no format change**. `Failed` and `Refused` keep nothing: a faulting body's ops are not trusted, and the runner commits a reply-only `Failed` itself. If the reply-only commit would pass `resident_limit`, the outcome is `Refused(c)` and nothing is kept. What it is worth: the runner's own control `no_d3_two_commits` (abort, then a separate reply-only commit) also has 0 failures (RUN: 4,441 states, 77 cuts). So D3 saves one commit per typed error and one round trip in the head; correctness does not depend on it. | §1.3, §1.8, L13 |
| F3 | N3: no wait for the admit ticket | **ACCEPTED (wording only)** | The journal is prefix-ordered (§3.3, and every model since v2 cuts only prefixes). A durable reply therefore implies a durable admit. `durable(admit ticket)` is needed only before an effect outside the store. | §1.8, L13 |
| F4 | `Superseded` and `Failed(Gone)` | **no store change: the smaller thing** | Superseded is a runner Outcome. Its proof is F1's `Rejected(l)` with `p < l`, so the store adds no `Admission` case. A gone position is answered by a `run` whose body only calls `reply(Failed(Gone))` and returns `Ok`. That is `Committed`, with a frame that has only a streams section. A re-send gets it back as `Duplicate`. The stream state holds no entry key, so nothing else is needed. (v2.24, AH2: the store no longer answers `Rejected(l)` with `p` < l, so it proves no `Superseded`.) | §1.8 |
| F5 | N4, `look` | **ACCEPTED with two changes** | (1) `look` runs the body in `isolate`, like `run`, so a faulting query cannot take the publisher down. It returns `Looked[R] = Seen(Seen[R]) \| Failed(Causes) \| Refused(Capacity)`, alike with `Outcome`. The runner's `Result[Looked[R], Error]` had no place for a fault. (2) **`fetch` and `range` take a `Shape`, not a `Table`.** `look` runs on the publisher task, and a `Table` is `send` but not shareable (it holds its index list). A query that must run under both `run` and `look` therefore reads through a `Shape` and an `Index`, both `shareable + send` (D1). Reads never needed a Table's index list or epoch; `put` and `delete` keep `Table`. RUN `programs-v23/`: a `scoped[view] fn(Tx) -> R` body over a view Tx is ACCEPTED (`look_view`). The same body calling `put(mut tx, …)` is REFUSED: OWN-5, "`tx` is not writable" (`look_put`). So "look cannot write" is the checker's rule; the store adds no run-time check. | §1.3, §1.5, §5 L22, §7 S1 |
| F6 | N5, `changes` | **ACCEPTED with three changes** | (1) Skips shared subtrees by **node id**, not Arc identity: within one open a node id names one immutable node, including nodes loaded from packs (§1.9), and `std.omap.node_id` is the landed view. (2) Returns `List[Change]` rather than `Rows`. `Rows` is one path with a `Key` and a `Codec`; a merge of two trees is neither. The runner asked for `Rows` but defined only `Change`. The list is charged to the caller's isolate, O(w). (3) `Foreign` only when the two Snapshots belong to different stores or **opens**; node ids are reissued after a reopen (§1.9). Different branches of one open are allowed: a fork shares nodes, so a diff across a fork costs O(w log n) too. Cost: O(k log n) node visits for k keys written between them, with w ≤ k returned (corrected in H4). The data tree only: a streams-only commit (F2, F4) has no change. | §1.5, §5 L23, §7 S1 |
| F7 | N6, a CALL section in COMMIT | **ACCEPTED, smaller** | **Format change, made before S2 lands:** COMMIT's section count becomes 1–3. Section tag 2 is `call`, at most one per COMMIT, and it has no ops count and no op tag, because it is not a tree. It carries: key (u32 length ‖ bytes), args (u32 length ‖ codec bytes) and stream (u32 length ‖ name). It drops the runner's `p` and `info`. `p` is the position in that stream's streams op in the same frame, which `record` requires (`Missing("reply")` otherwise). `CallInfo` is already derived from the frame's branch, version and `at` (§1.7). One fact, one place. **No new frame kind**: a separate kind could be torn away from its COMMIT; a section shares the frame's check. API: `CallRecord { key, args, stream }`; `record(mut tx, take c)`, where a second call is `Exists("call")` (no new Error case); `recorded(db, b, version) -> Option[CallRecord]`, served from live journal segments only. A commit whose segment a checkpoint has compacted reads as None, which RUNNER §7 reports as `Unknown(StateGone)`. Long retention is the tape's job, not the journal's. **Bytes:** the section is 1 + (4 + key) + (4 + args) + (4 + stream). With a 32-byte entry key (16 identity, 8 args_fp, 8 result_fp), 16 args bytes and an 8-byte stream name, that is **69 bytes**. A transact call that writes one row and replies 8 bytes is **205 bytes** (§2.4). The runner's form adds 4 (ops) + 1 (tag) + 8 (p) + 4 + CallInfo bytes (at least 28) on each recorded commit. Replay skips the section by its lengths and ignores it for state. **The model**: unchanged, because a section changes no frame boundary or cut. | §1.3, §2.4, §2.7, §5 L24, §7 S3, S5 |
| F8 | `follow` | **unchanged** | The runner releases only after `durable` (its G1), so `follow` need not be durable (RUNNER F8b). | — |
| F9 | the orchestrator's §2.4 initial values | **AGREED** | No conflict: index ids from `next_table` match §2.6's one counter and the catalog key prefix. Epoch 1 lets 0 mean "no Table" in `Stale`. Schema number 0 matches D1's u16 tag. | §2.4 |
| F10 | "the root's 32 bytes" | **already folded, re-verified** | §1.10's `Latest` row says 32 bytes. RUN at 1e866455: `crates/hirsel-core-layout/src/charge.rs:21` `LATEST_ROOT: u64 = 32`, asserted equal to `size_of::<Latest>()` in `hirsel-core-rt/src/latest.rs:21`. | §1.10 |
| F11 | the model (rules on streams and commits changed) | **re-run, clean** | `model_v23_streams.py` checks the store side alone: one stream, three positions, prefix-ordered crash cuts, and two crashes. **1,851 states, 2,396 crash cuts, 0 failures.** Its four mutants are all CAUGHT: `no_s7`, `abort_keeps_data`, `abort_drops_reply` and `abort_no_ticket`. The runner's calls model at this base gives 4,025 states, 63 cuts, 0 failures, and 6 of 6 mutants caught (5 plus `superseded_unchecked_store`). The frame model (`model_v22.py`: 122 cuts, 13 damage cases) is unchanged: F2's frame was already legal, and F7's section moves no boundary. | §3.9 |

## CHANGES-v2.2 (checksum ruling)

| # | Item | Verdict | What v2.2 does | Where |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | R9 measured by store-build-1010 on main: CRC-32C 266,801,271 instructions and 74.3 ms; xxh3-64 92,247,236 and 5.6 ms (10,000 × 4 KiB, LLVM release, both matching Rust). Orchestrator's ruling: xxh3-64 everywhere. | **ACCEPTED; my §2.1 guess was wrong** | xxh3-64 costs 2.25 instructions per byte against CRC-32C's 6.51, which is 2.9× fewer instructions and 13× less time. `int.mul_wide` exists, which removes the reason I gave. Every check in the format is now a u64 xxh3-64 (seed 0, default secret). It is the same checksum the compiler store and the tape use. The frame head is 16 bytes: kind u16, flags u16, len u32, check u64. | §2.1, §6 R9, §9 |
| E2 | what the check covers, and its binding | **bound to the store, the file and the offset** | `check = xxh3_64(identity[16] ‖ role u8 ‖ seq u64 ‖ offset u64 ‖ head[0,8) ‖ payload)`. That is the tape's rule (`xxh3(tape_id ‖ head ‖ payload)`) plus the frame's place. Role and seq are the file's, and offset is the frame's first byte in the file. A HEADER frame binds to the identity in its own payload; every other frame binds to its file's HEADER identity. | §2.1 |
| E3 | what the binding gains | — | **L12** gains a case: a whole, valid frame of this store at the wrong place (a misdirected write, a stale or duplicated sector, a NODE frame in the wrong pack) is `Corrupt(Checksum)`. Before, it decoded. For NODE frames this matters, because a duplicated node id is not otherwise refused (§2.8). **L19** gains frame granularity: a single frame spliced in from another store is refused at that frame, where v2 caught only whole files, by their HEADER. **L20 gains nothing**: its handles are in-memory values, not bytes. Cost: copy-forward recomputes the check of each node it moves (2.25 instructions per byte, measured). Journal frames, MANIFEST and END files are never moved. | §2.1, §3.5, §5 |
| E4 | detection is now probabilistic | **stated** | CRC-32C detects every error burst of 32 bits or less. A 64-bit hash misses any given damage with probability about 2⁻⁶⁴, single-byte flips included. L12's "gives `Corrupt`" now means "except with probability about 2⁻⁶⁴", as REPLAY-SPEC already states for the tape. | §2.8, L12 |
| E5 | byte figures | **recomputed** | A one-key COMMIT is **97 bytes** (was 93). A HEADER-only file is 72 bytes (was 68), so a segment's first `d` is 72. An END file is **96 bytes** (was 88). Each NODE frame on disk grows by 4 bytes. The resident row cost stays **118 B**: frame heads are not held in memory. | §2.3, §2.4, §3.2, §3.4, R4 |
| E6 | the model | **re-run, clean** | `model_v2.py` used a 12-byte head with CRC-32C. Its damage cases depend only on whether a check fails, not on its width. `model_v22.py` uses a 16-byte head with a 64-bit check (blake2b-8 standing in for xxh3, since Python here has no xxh3): **122 cuts, FAILED=0; 13 damage cases, FAILED=0** (RUN). It does not model the E2 binding, because no cut moves a frame; L12 and L19 test the binding on the real code. | §3.9 |
| E7 | library | **`std.check`** | `core/std/check.hirsel` holds one xxh3-64 implementation for all of std: the store, the tape, and anything later. Interface: a one-shot `xxh3(b: Bytes, lo: u64, hi: u64) -> u64`, and a streaming `Xxh3` state (`start`, `add(mut s, b, lo, hi)`, `finish`). A frame's check covers a prefix that is not in the file plus two separate ranges of the read buffer, so it needs the streaming form, and the ranges avoid a copy. `std.check.crc32c` is deleted. | §2.1, §7 S1 |

## 0. Summary

**Scope** (Sam, 2026-11-15 23:05):
- Rows 1–10 of M4-PLAN §2.3 are built now:
  1. typed tables, schemas and migrate;
  2. read sets;
  3. tickets and group commit;
  4. snapshots read on any task;
  5. CallInfo;
  6. call streams;
  7. KeyScope narrow (deleted in v2.30 AN1);
  8. pins;
  9. forks;
  10. incremental checkpoints.
- Rows 11 (claims and epoch fencing) and 12 (object-backed authorities) are specified for every authority by v2.46 (§12): the history head is the fence, and levels are per authority. §2.9 says what is still open.
- Rows 13 and 14 are never built:
  - a rename is a migrate;
  - internal state lives in its own trees and frame kinds, never in a reserved key space.
- There is one format. Its version is 1 and stays 1, and there is no migration from the old store.
- Checkpoints are incremental only.
- Rulings built in (orchestrator, 2026-11-15):
  - `channel.try_receive` is in core (907 builds it);
  - all state stays in memory for M4, under an admission bound;
  - the identity comes from `Random` (907).

**The design in one paragraph.**
- A store is one in-memory persistent B-tree of bytes per branch, in three trees: `data`, `streams` and `catalog`. The tree is 998's ordered map with `K = V = Bytes`, and its nodes are shared through `Arc`.
- A transaction body runs inside `isolate` on a path-copied working tree. Commit installs the new roots, so the commit is visible at once, and sends one `COMMIT` frame to a journal task.
- The journal task drains whatever is queued, writes it, syncs it and acknowledges it.
- A checkpoint task writes, to a new immutable pack, only the nodes no earlier pack holds. It then replaces `MANIFEST`, which names the packs, every branch and pin root, and the first live journal segment.
- Opening a store reads the manifest, the packs and the journal suffix, then starts a new journal segment. Nothing is ever appended to a file an earlier process wrote.

**The format in one diagram.**
```
<store dir>/
  LOCK                   empty; host.try_lock held by the one writer for the Db's life
  MANIFEST               HEADER(role 1) MANIFEST            replaced only by MANIFEST.tmp + sync + rename + sync_dir
  p-<seq:16 hex>         HEADER(role 3) NODE NODE ...       immutable pack; written .tmp, synced, renamed
  j-<seq:16 hex>         HEADER(role 2) COMMIT COMMIT ...   journal segment; append-only, one writer process
  j-<seq:16 hex>.end     HEADER(role 4) END(d)              the segment's synced end; rewritten whole by the journal task

every frame:  kind u16 | flags u16 (bit 0 = MUST) | len u32 | check u64 | payload[len]      (16-byte head, LE)
              check = xxh3_64(identity ‖ role ‖ seq ‖ offset ‖ head[0,8) ‖ payload)       (§2.1)

MANIFEST ── packs ─────────► p-*   ── NODE(id, level, entries) ── children by node id
         ── branches, pins ► (data, streams, catalog) root node ids + version
         ── first_live ────► j-<first_live>, j-<first_live+1>, ...   replayed in order on open
```

**Build order** (§7). There are six slices.

| Slice | Delivers | Needs | Starts |
|---|---|---|---|
| S0 | `std.codec`: `Codec[T]`, `Key[T]`, schema bytes, `resolve`, hand-written constructors | SEM-10 as landed | now |
| S1 | the in-memory store: `memory`, tables, indexes, `run`, read sets, cursors, CallInfo, snapshots, resident account | 998's map; S0's signatures | the day 998's map lands |
| S2 | on disk: packs, manifest, incremental checkpoint, GC, open and recovery, schema commits | S1; 998's constructors; 907 W1 (landed), W2 (extended), Random | after S1 |
| S3 | the journal: segments, END files, the journal task, tickets, group commit, poison, cancellation | S2; 907 `try_receive`, W2, W4 | after S2 |
| S4 | pins, forks, `adopt`, `migrate` | S2, S3 | after S3 |
| S5 | call streams (KeyScope `narrow` deleted in v2.30 AN1) | S3 | after S3, beside S4 |

**Open questions for Sam:** none. Q1 is ruled (try_receive), and so are memory and identity.

---

## 1. API

**Conventions.**
- Module `store`, in package `store`.
- Every declaration below has the shape of a probe the checker accepted (RUN, `programs/`, on 78e07cb1), unless it is marked otherwise.
- **Dictionaries are values.** A table takes `codec.Key[K]` and `codec.Codec[V]` values (S0, §7). It takes no `codec` bound.
  - RUN on 78e07cb1: the bound itself is still refused, `LANG-5 unknown bound` (`codec_bound`).
  - RUN: the same API taking dictionary values is accepted (`tx_body`).
  - Once the bound lands, a program passes `codec.of()` where it passes a hand-written value today. So the store's API is final from S1 and never waits for the derive.
  - Explicit type arguments at a call are refused (M4-PLAN §2.1), so a dictionary comes by annotation: `let c: codec.Codec[Account] = codec.of()`.
- **Every handle names its store.** `Table`, `Index`, `Branch`, `Snapshot`, `Ticket` and `CallId` carry the 16-byte `StoreId`. `Snapshot` and `Ticket` also carry the number of the Db's open (§1.12). A handle from another Db is `Foreign`. That is checked before any effect.

### 1.1 Opening and closing

```hirsel
pub type Options {
    create: bool,
    lock_wait_ms: u64,
    group_commits: u32,       // default 64: the most frames one journal write takes; 0 is Missing("group_commits") at open (W1)
    group_bytes: u32,         // default 4 MiB: the most bytes one journal write takes; 0 is Missing("group_bytes") at open (W1)
    checkpoint_bytes: u64,    // default 64 MiB of journal since the last cut starts a checkpoint
    pack_bytes: u64,          // default 64 MiB: a pack closes before a NODE that would take it past this many bytes, unless it holds no NODE yet (H1)
    resident_limit: u64,      // default 1 GiB (GUESS, R8): the accounted resident bytes a Db admits (§1.11)
    checkpoint_task_bytes: u64, // default 262,400,276: the checkpoint task's root limit, max(pack_bytes, 64 MiB + 88) + 2⌈resident_limit / 11⌉ + 64 KiB (Q1a)
    retain: u8,               // v2.47: CHECKPOINT entries in the retained set, 1–255, default 2, 0 is Missing("retain") (§12.6); objects@1 and sim@1 only
    checkpoint_entries: u64,  // v2.46: a cut runs when this many entries follow the latest CHECKPOINT, default 4096, at least 1 (§12.2)
    claim_ms: u64,            // v2.46: how long `open` retries a lost claim, local monotonic clock, default 30,000; 0 = one attempt (§12.3)
    head_poll_ms: u64,        // v2.46: the idle head poll's interval, default 1,000, at least 1 (§12.3)
    expect: Option[StoreId],  // v2.46: open only this store; another is `Foreign` before any write (§12.1)
    activation: Option[u64],  // v2.46: open only at this activation; another is `NotCurrent` before any write (§12.1)
    image: Option[Digest],  // v2.47: open only when the active image is this Describe digest; another is `NotCurrent` before any write (§12.1)
}
pub opaque type Authority   // v2.46 §12.1: the granted keeper of the history; config only, never a credential in program bytes
pub type StoreId { hi: u64, lo: u64 }
pub type Kind = Memory | Directory | Bucket(std.object.LaneConfig)
pub type Overrides { resident_limit: Option[u64], journal_limit: Option[u64], checkpoint_bytes: Option[u64], pack_bytes: Option[u64], group_bytes: Option[u64],
                      group_commits: Option[u32], lock_wait_ms: Option[u64],
                      cache_bytes: Option[u64], writer_pin_bytes: Option[u64], dirty_bytes: Option[u64], pager_task_bytes: Option[u64], readers: Option[u64] }   // v2.60: the Tiered plan (§1.1)
pub type Shortage { need: u64, have: u64, parts: List[(String, u64)] }
pub fn sized(kind: Kind, share: u64) -> Result[Options, Shortage]            // v2.57 DX Q6a: replaces defaults(); every byte figure derived from share
pub fn sized_with(kind: Kind, share: u64, o: Overrides) -> Result[Options, Shortage]   // each Some replaces its derived figure; the sum must still fit share
pub opaque type PlacePlan: send                                                // v2.76: sized Options, the writer plan and (Bucket) the capture; holds no heap storage beyond its Options
pub fn planned(kind: Kind, share: u64, o: Overrides) -> Result[PlacePlan, Shortage] // v2.76: replaces sized_reservation; planned_bytes(p) ≤ share
pub fn planned_options(p: PlacePlan) -> Options
pub fn planned_bytes(p: PlacePlan) -> u64                                           // T + X: the caller's whole store term
pub fn planned_capture(p: PlacePlan) -> Option[FollowerPlan]                           // Bucket: the capture's plan, F = T − L; other kinds None
pub opaque type WriterPlan: send                                               // v2.76: T, its lifetime terms and its maximizing phase
pub fn writer_plan(kind: Kind, o: Options) -> Result[WriterPlan, Shortage]    // the same pricing `planned` uses, for a caller that holds Options
pub fn writer_bytes(p: WriterPlan) -> u64                                      // T

pub opaque type Db                         // not send: holds Task handles (CONC-1/2). RUN db_task.
pub type Refusal { error: Error, authority: Authority }   // v2.70 D1: a failed open's error and the Authority it took, handed back whole
pub fn open(tasks: Tasks, take a: Authority, c: Clock, r: Random, o: Options) -> Result[Db, Refusal] waits   // v2.46: opens; a writer open of objects@1 or sim@1 claims (§12.3); v2.70: takes `a`, hands it back with every failure
pub fn close(take db: Db) -> Result[(), Error] waits   // §1.10: always consumes, always releases and joins
pub fn identity(db: Db) -> StoreId
```

**A failed open hands its Authority back (v2.70, D1).** `open` takes `a`. On success the Db owns the transport: on objects@1 the Client's `Workers` stay in the Db and its `Requests` endpoint moves into the journal task. **Every** failure returns `a` in `Refusal.authority`, whatever the `error` and wherever in §3.4 or §12.3 it arose, whether in §12.1's opening checks, recovery and admission, the claim loop, genesis, or after a won replace whose CLAIM advance failed:
- memory@1 hands back the value and log@1 its `Dir`. objects@1 hands back the same `std.object.Client`, never split, its lanes running, with the level and `op_ms` it was granted. sim@1 hands back the same way, with its `SimLevels`, its `LevelSync` and `op_ms` (v2.73).
- Before `open` returns, the attempt's tasks are joined (CONC-6/8), and every reservation it made is refunded (MEM-23): §12.9's fixed buffers, the journal and timer task limits, a claimant's private state. So the caller holds exactly what it held before the call, plus the error's own storage.
- The Authority carries no attempt state. The epoch, holder, position, tag and recovered state belong to the attempt and are dropped with it. Another `open` with the returned Authority claims afresh (§12.3), and a `follower` with it only reads (§12.5).

**Derived sizes (v2.57, DX Q6a).** `share` is the bytes this store may hold: the runner passes the executable's root limit minus `operate_bytes` minus main's 1 MiB keep (RUNNER-SPEC v2.45 §13). `sized` derives, in this order (all GUESS until measured, R8):
- `Memory`: `resident_limit` = share − 1 MiB, and no journal, pack or checkpoint figure is used.
- `Directory` and `Bucket`: `group_bytes` = 4 MiB, `pack_bytes` = min(64 MiB, share / 16), `checkpoint_bytes` = `pack_bytes`, `journal_limit` = `checkpoint_bytes` + `FRAME_LIMIT`, and the cut's working bound = 2⌈r / 11⌉ + 64 KiB (Q1a's term). `journal_limit` is the append rule's cap on uncovered journal bytes on disk (§3.4).
- **`Directory` (v2.75).** The grant is the writer's simultaneous peak: its **lifetime** terms plus the **largest** of three phases that never overlap. Lifetime: r; the journal worker, `group_bytes` + 64 KiB of grant plus its MEM-24 task charge 288 + 64 (it returns `Result[(), Error]`); the idle timer, 4 KiB + 288; and the six journal channels at their MEM-24 charges, 416g + 640 for g = `group_commits` (§3.4). Phases: **recovery** holds one 64 KiB input chunk and one checked frame, 64 KiB + `FRAME_LIMIT`; **write** holds a sealed frame while earlier frames up to `FRAME_LIMIT` wait for their ack (§3.4's in-flight bound), 2 × `FRAME_LIMIT`; a **cut** first drains every handed-off frame, then holds its output, max(`pack_bytes`, the MANIFEST file at its 16 MiB metadata limit = 16,777,640), and its working bound. `resident_limit` = r, the largest value with lifetime + max(recovery, write, cut) ≤ share. A `Shortage` itemizes the lifetime terms, r and the maximizing phase's terms, so `need` is still their sum. `journal_limit` is not a term: its bytes are on disk. v2.75 left the writer's fixed state unpriced. The writer plan below prices it.
- **The writer plan (v2.76).** `writer_plan(kind, o)` prices the grant that `open` makes for `o`. `planned` sizes with the same function, so one function owns T. Every term is a recipe applied to a type (MEM-33), and none is a literal:
  - **Journal channels.** The six channels of §3.4 are priced as `charge.channel(bytes[Item], capacity)`, one call per channel, with capacities 2g, 3g + 3, 1, 2, 1 and 1. At today's types that is 416g + 640, which is v2.75's figure.
  - **Worker and timer.** The journal worker is `charge.task(bytes[Result[(), Error]], group_bytes + 64 KiB)`, and the idle timer is `charge.task(bytes[()], 4 KiB)`.
  - **The writer's fixed state** is a new lifetime term, `writer_state`. At genesis the six empty pages and the four initial branch slots cost 1,872 B by MEM-24. The Db record is inline and the provider holds its mechanical file bookkeeping. Store's size law measures the retained writer charge after the 88 B startup channel is refunded.
  - **Growing metadata.** The location tables, the branch list and the pin list grow with what the store holds: one row per pack, per branch and per pin. They cannot go in r's resident account, because §1.11 recomputes that account from tree contents at each cut. Each growth is charged at its row's recipe size to the current limit of the Db call that grows it (MEM-26), which is the opening task's limit. A refusal is that call's `Full`, with nothing changed. The count is the live packs, branches and pins. **Open (v2.76):** no plan term covers these rows yet, so a caller budgets them beside T. The end state prices each list at a stated bound (a bound on packs from `retain` and compaction, and on branches and pins from new count limits) as a lifetime term. Choosing those bounds is a later STORE change.
  - **Phases.** Recovery, write and cut are as v2.75 states them. A cut's output is `cut_output_bytes`, max(`pack_bytes`, the MANIFEST file at its metadata limit). The cut phase also gains `CUT_STEP_BYTES` = 16,715,776, one step's copy into the paused writer's state (§13.8 "Each step's peak").
  - **`WriterPlan`** keeps T, its lifetime terms and the maximizing phase's terms. A `Shortage` lists the same parts.
- **The place plan (v2.76).** `planned(kind, share, o)` returns the `Options` that `sized_with(kind, share − X, o)` returns (for `Memory` and `Directory`, X = 0, so `sized_with(kind, share, o)`), together with:
  - X = 0 for `Memory` and `Directory`. For `Bucket`, X = `service_bytes([])` + `follower_starter_bytes()`, and `planned_capture` is the `FollowerPlan` of those `Options`.
  - `planned_bytes`, which is T + X. This equals max(T, L + `service_bytes([capture])` + `follower_starter_bytes()`), because F = T − L.
  - **How the share is solved.** Store solves for T + X ≤ `share`, so X comes out of the share inside Store, never in a caller.
  - **Shortage.** A `Shortage` itemizes X's two parts beside T's parts.
  - **What a caller does.** A caller multiplies `planned_bytes` by the number of stores it holds at once and adds its own terms, and does nothing else with a Store figure (MEM-33 "Who computes what").
- **`Bucket` (v2.78).** As for Directory, r is the largest value with lifetime + max(recovery, write, cut) ≤ the writer's share. The lifetime terms are r, fixed writer state, journal channels, and §12.9's lane reservation, journal workspace, timer and worker (with its reclaim page).
  - **Recovery.** A fetched entry and one decoded frame, or the checkpoint packet and one pack read, whichever is larger. Suffix and location tables are charged where they grow (§12.9).
  - **Journal write.** One staged frame and up to `FRAME_LIMIT` of frames awaiting journal acknowledgment. The worker uses its own grant and the §12.9 workspace for the history packet and comparisons.
  - **Cut.** After draining journal frames, the writer takes the journal session and keeps its workspace while the cut uses a second one. The cut holds one output of up to max(`pack_bytes`, the MANIFEST file bound), two head buffers, a key, a packet large enough for the locator root and retained checkpoint references, and a comparison buffer large enough for the output. Its upload room covers the greater of one multipart part with its list slot and the encoded MANIFEST, which occur in separate steps. Add the per-node working bound and `CUT_STEP_BYTES` (§13.8). A `Shortage` lists the lifetime and maximizing phase terms.
  - `journal_limit` sets the uncovered-history limit. `Bucket` carries the lane configuration passed to `std.object.start`, including its default-lane selection.
- `group_commits` keeps its listed default of 64 and `lock_wait_ms` defaults to 0 unless explicitly overridden. The other count fields (`retain`, `checkpoint_entries`, `claim_ms`, `head_poll_ms`) keep their listed defaults. `create`, `expect`, `activation` and `binding` are the caller's.
- **The Tiered plan (v2.60, astra 1995 #14).** The Tiered figures are carved out of r, never added beside it, because §13.8's resident account already holds `cache_bytes`. Let V = `VALUE_LIMIT`, Wmin = 2V + 1 MiB, and U the sum of the Reader reservations the caller will make (`Overrides.readers`, default one Reader of V + 1 MiB; each at least V + 1 MiB, §13.3). For an integer q from Wmin through 64 MiB: `writer_pin_bytes` W = q, `dirty_bytes` D = q and `pager_task_bytes` P = ⌈q / 4⌉, and `cache_bytes` C is sized from the remainder (v2.76, below). These weights are GUESS defaults (R8). At q = 64 MiB and r ≥ 439,374,696, they are §13.8's listed values. An override replaces its own field before solving, W in C's floor included. The plan requires W ≥ Wmin, C ≥ W + U and §13.8's resident floor r ≥ C + K + D + P + 64 MiB, with K, D and P counted once and the writer and reader pins inside C, never again. K = `CUT_PIN_BYTES` = 19,944,296 is the cut pin quota (v2.74, §13.8). It is a constant of the format, derived from the cut's access path. It is not an `Overrides` or `Options` field, and it does not depend on q. `sized` picks the largest feasible q; Memory rows get what remains of r. When no q is feasible, `sized` sets the four fields to 0 and the store can hold no Tiered collection: `open` of a catalog with one is `Missing("cache_bytes")`, and a promotion is refused as below, each before anything is reserved or claimed. C is reserved once with its partitions, K once as the backing of the pager's cut-pinned frames, D with the replaced list (§13.6), and P for the pager. A pager GET's frames land in C, or in K for a cut's demand. Its range buffer is the pager's own (§13.11). Neither has a term of its own.
- **The cache from the remainder (v2.76; replaces C = max(4q, W + U)).** C has a guaranteed part and an optional part:
  - **The floor is the guarantee.** For q, the floor is f(q) = (W + U) + K + D + P + 64 MiB. That is 2.25q, rounded up through P, plus U + K + 64 MiB, so f increases strictly in q. A q is feasible when W ≥ Wmin and f(q) ≤ r, and feasibility is monotone in q, so `sized` binary-searches it as before and picks the largest feasible q.
  - **The cache is what remains, up to its target.** C = max(W + U, min(4q, r − K − D − P − 64 MiB)). The upper bound 4q is the old tuning target, now a ceiling instead of a floor. The Memory rows keep the 64 MiB floor and everything above C, so the cache and the Memory rows never claim the same byte.
  - **Overrides.** An override of `cache_bytes` replaces C and must still be at least W + U and fit f. An override of W moves W + U with it.
  - **Every outstanding pin grant is protected.** C ≥ W + U holds at every r, so the writer's W and each Reader's reservation (§13.3) keep their partitions in full. The part of C above W + U is the shared unpinned side (§13.2), which no grant and no cut pins.
  - **The default floor.** At q = Wmin = 2 × 16,711,680 + 1,048,576 = 34,471,936, with one default Reader U = 17,760,256: C = 52,232,192, K = 19,944,296, D = 34,471,936, P = 8,617,984, and the Memory floor is 67,108,864. The sum is **182,375,272**, against 268,030,824 when C was 4q = 137,887,744. Above the floor q grows faster than before, because f(q) is about 2.25q where it was about 6.25q. q reaches 64 MiB at r = 255,808,360, where it used to need 439,374,696. Between those two figures W, D and P are larger than v2.75 gave and C is smaller. At r = 268,030,824, W and D move from 34,471,936 to 67,108,864 and C from 137,887,744 to 97,091,584. From 439,374,696 up every figure is unchanged.
  - **No per-slot term.** No plan figure depends on a slot or row count, so M3 S5 can drop its 24 B/slot exact-growth accounting without moving the floor.
- **Which plan.** `open` selects the plan from the recovered catalog (or, at genesis, the schema it is about to declare) before it reserves anything or claims a Bucket. A store with no Tiered collection reserves zero cache, dirty and pager bytes and starts no pager, so its Memory rows get all of r. The first Memory → Tiered `set_residency` is admitted against the Tiered plan before it changes anything: the Memory rows already resident plus C + K + D + P + 64 MiB must fit r, else `Full(Resident(Capacity { requested, available: r }))` with nothing changed. On a memory store Tiered is `Tiered(Memory)` (§13.8) and the plan is the non-Tiered one.
- **Checked arithmetic.** The root subtraction and every sum above are checked; an overflow or a negative remainder is the `Shortage` below (in `sized`) or the refusal above (at `open` and promotion), never a wrapped figure.
- `sized` refuses when r would be below 1 MiB or any floor (`journal_limit` ≥ `checkpoint_bytes` + `FRAME_LIMIT`,) fails: `Shortage{need, have: share, parts}`, where `parts` names each figure with its bytes and `need` is their sum at the floors. With `Overrides`, a `Some` figure replaces its derived value, and the remaining derived figures are computed after it; a sum past `share` is the same `Shortage`. There are no named profiles, and the "default" comments above are the figures for share = 2 GiB.

**A follower's plan (v2.69 B, MEM-30).**

```hirsel
pub opaque type FollowerPlan: send                                            // effective Options, the kind and F; computing or copying it reserves nothing
pub fn follower_plan(kind: Kind, o: Options) -> Result[FollowerPlan, Shortage]
pub fn plan_bytes(p: FollowerPlan) -> u64                                     // F
pub fn service_bytes(plans: List[FollowerPlan]) -> Option[u64]                // S + the sum of F; None on overflow
pub fn follower_starter_bytes() -> u64                                         // v2.70 D2: the starter's charge outside `bytes` (§12.5 "The starter's charges"); 1,098 at the current build's types
```

- **Which fields.** The plan keeps `o`'s size and count fields, and **holds no heap storage** (v2.70, D2): no String or Bytes content of `o` is copied into it, so copying or cloning a plan allocates nothing. `create`, `activation` and `image` select a writer and are ignored, and `expect` is `follower`'s own argument, so the plan ignores `o.expect`.
- **The service's limit.** A `FollowerService` started with `bytes` provisions slots inside that limit. S is the service's own fixed storage: its request channel and its loop state, each at its MEM-24 logical size. `service_bytes` returns S plus the sum of the plans' F with checked arithmetic, which is the `bytes` that lets every listed plan hold a slot at once; a smaller `bytes` is legal, and a slot it cannot fit is refused as below.

- **T and L.** T is the checked total of the parts above at `o`'s figures for `kind` (for `Directory`, v2.75's lifetime terms plus its largest phase, priced by v2.76's writer plan): the figure `sized` and `sized_with` compare with `share`, and the parts a `Shortage` itemizes. For `Directory` L = 0. For `Bucket`, L is exactly the `client_lanes` part at `o`'s lane configuration. The follower envelope is **F = T − L**. A follower's transport is the authority's: it was started with its own reservation under its own owner, and moving its `Requests` endpoint into a worker resets no inherited bound, so any transport workers it depends on are started under their owner at startup too. L is the sizing term removed from T, not a claim that the transport costs L. A deployment budgets each transport once at its owner and F once per provisioned follower, and a caller planning several followers fits their sum and its other live charges at the service's limit.
- **The holder-derived total (open item, v2.69 B).** F uses the holder's parts, so the journal, timer, cut and PUT terms enlarge the envelope although a follower creates none of those objects and reserves nothing a second time for them. The `Shortage` and `Overrides` rules above apply with their floors. F is fixed by the plan, however much room the service has. A tighter default needs a follower sizing law of its own.
- **Q and N.** Q is the fixed per-slot control storage at the service: one capacity-one command channel (64 + the command's logical size, MEM-24) and the MEM-24 charge of the service's entry that holds the worker's Task handle and retirement notification, each at its logical size and in fixed per-slot storage, so a growing registry cannot consume another slot's grant. Replies use a capacity-one channel per request, charged to the requester. All other worker control storage is made inside the worker. The worker returns `()`, so its MEM-24 task charge is 288 + N, and its root limit is **N = F − Q − 288**. Every product, sum and difference is checked. When Q + 288 > F, `follower_plan` returns `Shortage{need: Q + 288, have: F, parts}` with both parts itemized.
- **What N pays.** Every allocation the worker makes draws on N (§12.9), including a Tiered follower's pager task and its cache, which are the worker's children. A Reader's pin partition already inside that cache adds no reservation (§13.4). `resident_limit` stays AP15's separate logical ceiling, carried in the plan's Options (§12.5 "Resident memory").

`open` takes `Random` for the identity: 16 bytes from `host.random(r, mut b)` (host.hirsel:31, landed 1951a976), drawn once at genesis (D7).

```hirsel
pub type Error =
      Held                         // another writer holds LOCK (log@1; objects@1 has no Held, a later claim deposes, §12.3)
    | NotFound                     // no MANIFEST (log@1) or no head (objects@1) and create is false; or no head while `o.expect` or `o.activation ≠ 0` is set (§12.1)
    | Corrupt(Fault)               // bytes from disk failed a check (§2.8)
    | Unsupported(u64)             // a format number other than 1, or an unknown MUST kind (value = kind)
    | Io(IoError)                  // a host operation failed before anything was published
    | Poisoned(IoError)            // a write or a sync failed earlier; the Db accepts only close
    | Full(Capacity)               // resident_limit: an open, a schema commit or a committing admit would pass it (§1.11, AE3)
    | Limit(Limit)
    | Schema(u64)                  // codec.resolve: the stored writer schema does not resolve; offset into it (SEM-10)
    | Stale(u32)                   // a handle's id is not live in the catalog it reads (I3), or the write Tx's registry lacks the table id (§1.2)
    | Conflict(String)             // v2.57 DX Q3: a Unique index entry is owned by another key (index name); the Tx is abort-only after it (§1.2)
    | Changed(String)              // v2.57 DX Q1: Open or Follower: an index's kind or its extractor's or projection's revision differs from the catalog's (index name)
    | Undeclared(String)           // v2.57 DX Q1: a catalog table or index that the declaration does not name (§1.2)
    | Decode(codec.DecodeError)    // a stored row failed its codec: only a schema bug in user code
    | Exists(String) | Missing(String)
    | Diverged(u32)                // adopt: main moved after the branch forked (branch id)
    | Foreign                      // a handle of another store, or a Snapshot or Ticket of another open (§1.12); an authority that holds another store (§12.1)
    | Fenced(u64)                  // another holder's bytes are in the head; the value is this holder's epoch. Whether an outstanding group applied is unknown until the next claim (§12.3)
    | Lost                         // open's claim lost: another claimant won, a genesis race was lost, or `claim_ms` ran out (§12.3)
    | Retired                      // follower worker or service endpoint closed (§12.5, v2.71)
    | Undecided                    // a head write's outcome stayed unknown after the Q5 rule; the claim is dead and only a later claim decides (§12.3)
    | Remote(std.object.Error)     // an authority request failed before any byte of it could have applied; the holder stops until reopened (§12.3)
    | NoLevel(String)              // the authority declares no level of this name (§12.4)
    | Declared(String)             // the grant's level declaration differs from the store's at this level name; nothing written (§12.1, §12.4)
    | NotCurrent(u64)              // `Options.activation` differs from the head's; the value is the head's (§12.1)
    | Endpoint(EndpointRefusal)    // v2.77: the endpoint cannot hold the store: Insecure | Unproven | NotSimulator | IgnoresIfNoneMatch | IgnoresIfMatch (§12.2)
    | Behind(Position)             // a follower reached its deadline; the value is its applied Position on that branch (§12.5)
    | Gone(u32)                    // the branch of a Position was deleted or adopted (§12.5)
    | Unseen(u32)                  // v2.47: a follower's deadline passed before it applied the branch's creation (§12.5)
    | Missed                       // v2.59: a latched Cold miss inside a body attempt (§13.3); seen only by the body, never returned from run, serve or look
    | Reclaimed(u64)               // a follower needed an object that reclaim removed; the value is the new floor (§12.5, §12.6)
pub type Limit = Key | Value | Transaction | Name
pub type Fault { file: String, offset: u64, why: Why }
pub type Why = Checksum | Truncated | Flags | Kind(u64) | Header | Gap(u64) | Order | Dangling(u64) | Malformed | Absent   // Absent (v2.46): a named object that is still live is missing (§12.5)
```

There is **no `Cancelled` case.** A cancellation is a failure that `isolate` does not catch, so it never reaches a caller as a value (C5, §3.7).

**Limits.** These are fixed at creation and recorded in the manifest. The values are the old store's (STORE-RECORD.md, BY READING):

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| tree key (table prefix included) | 4096 bytes |
| value | 1 MiB |
| one transaction's COMMIT payload (the frame's `len`, head excluded) | 16 MiB + 64 = 16,777,280 bytes in a store with a journal; the one transaction limit, the same as §2.7's COMMIT row (U1). A `memory` store has no frame and no transaction size limit: its resident account (§1.11) and the caller's byte bound limit a transaction (v2.55, Spec Q4) |
| branch, pin and table names | 255 bytes |
| fan-out | 16–32 entries per node (998's occupancy) |

The old limit of 10,000 rows per range is dropped: a cursor needs no limit.

### 1.2 Tables and indexes

v2.57 (DX Q1, Q3): one handle per table, and index extractors live in a registry. `Shape`, `shape`, `spec`, `with_index`, `TableSpec`, `create_table`, `create_index`, `table`, `index` and the store-level `migrate`/`drop_table` are deleted. A program declares its schema through `Declare`, and changes its catalog only through `Migration` in `Migrate` mode.

```hirsel
pub opaque type Readers[V]: shareable + send   // Codec[V], current schema number, List[Option[codec.Reader[V]]] by number
pub opaque type Table[K, V]: shareable + send  // StoreId, table id, catalog key, Key[K], Arc[Readers[V]]: reads and writes; no extractors, no epoch
pub opaque type Index[J, K, V, P]: shareable + send // StoreId, index id, catalog key, kind, owning table id, Key[J], Key[K], Arc[Readers[V]], Arc[Readers[P]]
pub type IndexKind = Many | Unique

pub type Mode = Migrate | Open | Follower
pub opaque type Declare                          // not send: the mode, the captured base, the staged catalog, the index registry being built, the names declared
pub opaque type TableDecl[K, V]                  // not send: a table being declared; unusable for reads and writes until `finish`
pub fn declare_table[K, V](mut d: Declare, name: String, take key: codec.Key[K], take value: codec.Codec[V]) -> Result[TableDecl[K, V], Error]
pub fn index[J, K, V](mut d: Declare, mut t: TableDecl[K, V], name: String, kind: IndexKind,
        by: StaticFn[fn(K, V) -> Result[List[J], Capacity]], take key: codec.Key[J]) -> Result[Index[J, K, V, ()], Error]
pub fn covering[J, K, V, P](mut d: Declare, mut t: TableDecl[K, V], name: String, kind: IndexKind,
        by: StaticFn[fn(K, V) -> Result[List[J], Capacity]], take key: codec.Key[J],
        project: StaticFn[fn(K, V) -> Result[P, Capacity]], take payload: codec.Codec[P]) -> Result[Index[J, K, V, P], Error]
pub fn covering_row[J, K, V](mut d: Declare, mut t: TableDecl[K, V], name: String, kind: IndexKind,
        by: StaticFn[fn(K, V) -> Result[List[J], Capacity]], take key: codec.Key[J]) -> Result[Index[J, K, V, V], Error]   // the identity projection
pub fn finish[K, V](mut d: Declare, take t: TableDecl[K, V]) -> Result[Table[K, V], Error]
pub fn declare(db: Db, mode: Mode) -> Result[Declare, Error]             // Migrate or Open; Follower is `declare_follower`
pub fn declare_follower(f: Follower) -> Declare
pub fn seal(mut db: Db, take d: Declare) -> Result[Ticket, Error] waits  // Migrate: the one schema commit; Open: checks undeclared names, commits nothing
pub fn seal_follower(f: Follower, take d: Declare) -> Result[(), Error]  // checks undeclared names at the captured base

pub opaque type Migration                        // not send: made for `on_migrate` only, in Migrate mode (AL4)
pub fn migrate_table[K, V, K2, V2](mut m: Migration, from: String, take key: codec.Key[K], take value: codec.Codec[V],
        to: String, take key2: codec.Key[K2], take value2: codec.Codec[V2],
        f: fn(K, V) -> Result[Option[(K2, V2)], Capacity]) -> Result[(), Error]
pub fn drop_table(mut m: Migration, name: String) -> Result[(), Error]
pub fn rename_table(mut m: Migration, from: String, to: String) -> Result[(), Error]
```

A `mut` lend lasts for one call (OWN-7, OWN-8), so `declare` captures a private base through a view. `seal` takes a fresh mutable lend and checks the exact base before publishing.

**The registry (DX Q1, Fable 5).** Each `Db` and each `Follower` owns one index registry: a map from table id to the erased extractors and projections of that table's indexes, in declaration order. Each entry is an owning `own[send] fn(K, V) -> Result[(List[Bytes], Bytes), Capacity]` that returns the sorted, deduplicated encoded keys and the encoded payload. `seal` installs it. A write `Tx` made by `run`, `run_on` or `serve` borrows the registry of its `Db` for its lifetime. `put` and `delete` look up the table id there, once per call. A table id the registry lacks (a `Table` from another `Declare` of this open) is `Stale(id)`. So there is no epoch: the catalog and the registry change together, at `seal`, and a handle names only an id. A `Follower`'s registry has no extractors, and its Tx cannot be a write Tx.

**What `Declare` does, by mode.**
- The catalog entry of a table holds its name, its key schema, its value schema list (D1, below) and, for each index, the index's:
  - name, kind, key schema and payload schema list;
  - `code.identity` and `code.revision` of `by`, and of `project` if it has one, both 32-byte values. `covering_row` stores the table's own schema list as its payload schemas and no projection.
- On a disk store, a declaration whose `code.revision` is unavailable is `Missing("revision")`. A memory store stores the revision as absent and compares identities alone. PROG-9's revision covers the function's whole reachable checked IR, so it sees a body edit that the identity keeps.
- **`Migrate`** stages, in order:
  1. `on_migrate`'s `Migration` operations;
  2. each declared table: created if absent, and a new value schema appended if it resolves (D1);
  3. each declared index: created if absent, rebuilt if its kind, key schema, payload schema or either revision differs, kept otherwise;
  4. each catalog index of a declared table that is not declared: dropped;
  5. each catalog table outside the reserved `hirsel.` namespace that is not declared and was not dropped or renamed in step 1: `Undeclared(name)`, and nothing commits.
  
  `seal` publishes all of it in one schema commit (§3.5), at version + 1. A refusal at any step changes nothing.
- **`Open`** checks without writing. An absent table or index is `Missing(name)`, a different key or payload schema is `Schema(0)`, a different kind or revision is `Changed(name)`, a value schema the stored list lacks is `Missing("schema")` (only Migrate appends), and a catalog index or app table the declaration does not name is `Undeclared(name)`, reported by `seal`. So a release whose identity matches its store (RUNNER-SPEC §6) always opens.
- **`Follower`** makes `Open`'s checks over the follower's applied catalog. It replaces `follower_table` and `follower_index`, which are deleted.
- **Names.** A repeated table or index name within one `Declare` is `Exists(name)`. The reserved `hirsel.` namespace is the runner's and the projector's; an application name in it is `Missing(name)`.

**Index entries (DX Q3).** A `Many` entry is `ix u32 BE ‖ J ‖ K => payload`. A `Unique` entry is `ix u32 BE ‖ J => u32 LE len(K) ‖ K ‖ payload`. A payload is empty for `()`. Otherwise it is `u16 LE schema number ‖ codec bytes`, numbered by the index's own append-only payload schema list and read through its own `Readers[P]`, transcoded to the current P like a row (D1). A `covering_row` payload is the row's stored bytes, schema number included. The extractor's list is sorted by encoded bytes and deduplicated before staging. Extraction, sorting, deduplication, payload encoding and comparison, conflict probes and edit planning all run inside the write's byte and step bounds (MEM-19, MEM-30), with identical steps whether or not roots are retained (AP15's law extended: L74). A many-key extractor that returns n keys costs O(n log n) of the write's steps, duplicates included. An unchanged encoded key with byte-equal payload bytes is not rewritten. A changed payload at an unchanged key is rewritten. Each index entry is charged as its own row version (`62 + r8(key) + r8(value)`, §1.11) and its own COMMIT op bytes. No payload bytes are shared between a row and its covering entries, or between two indexes.

**Unique writes (DX Q3, Astra 9, Fable 11, 15).** `put(mut tx, t, k, v)` and `delete(mut tx, t, k)` build the complete edit before staging any part of it:
- the old row, from the staged view;
- each index's old and new key sets, with their payloads;
- the primary edit;
- the COMMIT op bytes and the resident charge (§1.1 limits, §1.11).

Then, for each `Unique` index in declaration order and each J in the new set but not the old (encoded order), it probes the staged view of `ix ‖ J`. An entry whose K differs from k is `Conflict(index name)`. A successful put records `Point(ix ‖ J)` for each probe. A transaction limit, `Limit(Key)` or `Limit(Value)` is found in the same preflight. Only a complete edit is staged. On any error nothing of it is staged, and on `Conflict` the Tx becomes **abort-only**:
- Every later `put` or `delete` in it returns the first `Conflict` with nothing staged, and reads continue.
- If the body returns `Error(a)`, F2 applies (the data is undone and a reply is kept).
- If the body returns `Ok(r)`, `run` and `run_on` answer `Failed(StoreFailure.Conflict(name))` and commit nothing, and `serve` answers `Failed(p, Conflict(name))`, which the runner concludes as `Failed(Conflict(name))` (RUNNER-SPEC v2.45 §1.1).
- A conflict that a helper swallows therefore cannot commit the writes before it.
- Delete and re-insert in one Tx is not a conflict, because the probe reads the staged view. To swap two rows' unique keys, delete one row, put the other, then put the first.
- `Stop` gains `Conflict(String)`. Re-execution compares it like any `Failed` reply.

**Backfill (Fable 12).** `Migrate` builds a created or rebuilt index from the table's rows at the seal's base. It reads the table in key order in chunks of at most 4,096 rows. It extracts each chunk into a sorted run charged to the migration's allowance, and merges the runs into a bottom-up build (§11.9). For a `Unique` index, the merge compares adjacent J and refuses the first duplicate with `Conflict(name)`. The build is admitted against `resident_limit` before it starts (§1.11), and every refusal leaves the old catalog and rows. The whole migration commits in its one cut. `migrate_table`'s rows are built the same way, and the indexes the declaration names for the target are built from the new rows. No extractor of the old table is applied to a new value (AB1).

**Read handles (I3).** A table or index id names one incarnation: ids come from the `next_table` counter and are never reused, so a table recreated after `drop_table`, or migrated, has a new id.
- Every read (`fetch`, `range`, `count`, `lookup`, `entries`, the prefix forms, and the `Reader` forms of §1.5, also inside `look`) first looks up the handle's catalog key in the catalog tree of the roots it reads: the Tx's roots, or the Snapshot's. If the key is absent, or holds another id, the read is `Stale(id)`, with nothing read and nothing recorded. A catalog root byte-identical to the one-leaf root the handle was resolved against answers without the lookup (I3).
- So a handle from before a drop is `Stale` against a current Tx or a later Snapshot, and reads its rows from a Snapshot or pin older than the drop. A handle made after the drop is `Stale` against that older Snapshot.
- Cost: one catalog lookup per read call, not per row.

**Value schemas (D1).**
- **Schema numbers.** Each table's catalog entry lists the value schemas its rows were written in, as (number u16, schema bytes, fingerprint). The list is append-only, and a number is never reused. Every row value starts with its schema number (§2.4).
- `declare_table` computes the program's value schema (`codec.schema`) and finds it in the list (fingerprint, then bytes):
  - **found** as number n: n becomes the Table's current number, and new rows are written as n;
  - **not found:** in `Migrate`, it is appended as the next number and becomes current; in `Open` and `Follower` it is `Missing("schema")`.
- Every other live number m is resolved once: `codec.resolve(value, schema_m)`, which applies SEM-10 (fields matched by name at every depth; a field the writer lacks takes its literal default; a removed field's tombstone checked).
  - Any `Schema(i)` makes `declare_table` return `Schema(i)`. `i` is the offset into schema m.
  - The Readers are shared by one `Arc`, so a copy of a Table or Index never resolves again.
- **Reading a row:** tag = current number, then `codec.decode`. Tag = an older number, then `codec.read` with that number's Reader. A tag the Readers do not hold is `Stale(table id)`.
- The key schema must be byte-equal to the stored one. A change of key order is always `Schema`, and only `migrate_table` fixes it.
- `migrate_table` writes every row as one new number and retires all older ones. It is the only way to drop an old schema. It gives the table, and each of its indexes, a new id (I3).

**Schema commits.** `seal` in `Migrate` is the only schema commit. A checkpoint makes it (§3.5), never a journal frame.
- It advances the branch version by one, so an unchanged version means nothing was committed (K1). A `seal` that finds nothing to change commits nothing and leaves the version unchanged. The runner's rule 12 relies on this.
- The catalog therefore changes only at a manifest swap, and every journal suffix is decoded under one catalog.
- `seal` admits its new trees against `resident_limit` before building them, using their accounted size (§1.11), else `Full`.
- Cost: a schema commit costs one checkpoint, which is 7 syncs (§3.2). Schema commits are rare.
- **Format.** The index kind, payload schema list and revisions are catalog fields of Format 5 (STORE-SPEC M3). A store whose catalog lacks them is `Unsupported(format)`, with no migration.

### 1.3 Transactions

```hirsel
pub opaque scoped type Tx                // VERIFY-5 B2: opaque (PROG-2). Base roots (views), working roots, op list, read Log view, scope, CallInfo
pub type StoreFailure = Raised(Causes) | Conflict(String)
pub type Outcome[R, A] = Committed(Done[R]) | Aborted(Undone[A]) | Failed(StoreFailure) | Refused(Capacity) | Stopped(core.OutOfTime)   // AC1
pub type Undone[A] { value: A, ticket: Option[Ticket] }   // F2: the ticket of the kept reply commit, if any
pub type Done[R] { value: R, ticket: Ticket, info: CallInfo, reads: List[Read] }
pub type Read = Point(Bytes) | Span(Bytes, Bytes)   // data-tree keys (§2.4), the bytes of Change.tree_key; span [lo, hi) (I1)
pub type Bound[K] = Unbounded | Included(K) | Excluded(K)   // std.omap's names (D9); K need not be ordered

pub fn run[R, A](mut db: Db, steps: Option[u64], body: scoped[view] fn(mut Tx) -> Result[R, A]) -> Result[Outcome[R, A], Error] waits   // None: no step scope (AC1); v2.59 §13.3: plain fn + inert env, and None is Missing("steps") on a retry-capable call
pub fn run_on[R, A](mut db: Db, b: Branch, steps: Option[u64], body: scoped[view] fn(mut Tx) -> Result[R, A]) -> Result[Outcome[R, A], Error] waits

pub fn fetch[K, V](tx: Tx, t: Table[K, V], k: K) -> Result[Option[V], Error]       // a fresh value; F5
pub fn put[K, V](mut tx: Tx, t: Table[K, V], k: K, v: V) -> Result[(), Error]
pub fn delete[K, V](mut tx: Tx, t: Table[K, V], k: K) -> Result[bool, Error]
pub fn range[K, V](tx: Tx, t: Table[K, V], lo: Bound[K], hi: Bound[K]) -> Result[TxRows[K, V], Error]   // v2.59: stepped by next_in (§13.4)
pub fn range_prefix[K, V, Q](tx: Tx, t: Table[K, V], q: Q, take prefix: codec.Key[Q]) -> Result[TxRows[K, V], Error]   // v2.57: keys whose leading components equal q
pub fn count[K, V](tx: Tx, t: Table[K, V], lo: Bound[K], hi: Bound[K]) -> Result[u64, Error]   // v2.57: one Span, O(log N) (AP11 subtree counts)
pub fn lookup[J, K, V, P](tx: Tx, ix: Index[J, K, V, P], lo: Bound[J], hi: Bound[J]) -> Result[IndexRows[K, V], Error] in tx   // J1: scoped to the Tx
pub fn lookup_prefix[J, K, V, P, Q](tx: Tx, ix: Index[J, K, V, P], q: Q, take prefix: codec.Key[Q]) -> Result[IndexRows[K, V], Error] in tx
pub fn entries[J, K, V, P](tx: Tx, ix: Index[J, K, V, P], lo: Bound[J], hi: Bound[J]) -> Result[IndexEntries[J, K, P], Error] in tx   // v2.57: index-only (J, K, P), no join
pub fn info(mut tx: Tx) -> CallInfo      // mut: only a transaction body has CallInfo; a look body cannot call it (G2, OWN-5)
pub type CallRecord: codec { key: Bytes, args: Bytes, stream: Bytes, revision: Option[Bytes], code: Bytes }   // F7; p and CallInfo come from the frame; revision: code.revision of the entry that ran; v2.30 AN1: code = u64 n ‖ u64 s (BE) ‖ replay identity (0 or 32 B)
pub type Plan { n_e: u64, s_e: u64, reply_max: u64 }   // v2.30 AN1: the body's byte and step allowances, and the longest reply
pub type Stop = Raised(u32) | OutOfSteps(u64) | OutOfBytes(Capacity) | Conflict(String)   // v2.30 AN1: Policy deleted; v2.57: Ok from an abort-only Tx (§1.2)
pub type Served = Committed(Receipt) | Kept(Receipt) | Failed(Pending, Stop) | NoRoom(Pending, Capacity)   // v2.56 §13.3: NoRoom may carry Cache; v2.29 AM1, AM3; ATTACK-4 B7: the refusal's Capacity
pub type Receipt { ticket: Ticket, reply: Bytes }   // v2.29 AM3: the first delivery, no read-back; v2.30 AN1
pub type ServeError = Before(Error) | After(Error)   // v2.29 AM4: Before leaves the position as it was; After is poison
pub opaque type Pending   // v2.29 AM1: not copy, codec or send; the Completion, the record, the run's CallInfo and base, and on NoRoom the outcome it would have stored
pub fn serve(mut db: Db, take c: Completion, plan: Plan, take rec: Option[CallRecord],
        body: scoped[view] fn(mut Tx) -> Result[Bytes, Bytes]) -> Result[Served, ServeError] waits   // v2.59 §13.3: plain fn + inert env; v2.30 AN1: one isolated execution, the body's; with `conclude`, the only writer of a reply and a record
pub fn conclude(mut db: Db, take p: Pending, take r: Bytes, reserve: Reserve) -> Result[Served, ServeError] waits   // v2.29 AM1, AM6: r with p's record, CallInfo and base, one streams-only commit, no code run; Reserve = Resident | Claim
pub fn untried(take c: Completion, take rec: Option[CallRecord], info: CallInfo) -> Pending   // v2.29 AM1: for a position that runs nothing (a gone key)
pub fn recorded(db: Db, b: Branch, version: u64) -> Result[Option[Recorded], Error] waits   // write barrier, then live segments; None once a taken cut covers the version (W2); v2.29 AM6 (ATTACK-4 M3): with its settle context
pub type StopKind = Raised | OutOfSteps(u64) | OutOfBytes | Conflict   // v2.59: settle 1's typed stop (format 5, AP1a)
```
